A.explanation: Too small by a factor of about 30. It does not follow from $v = p/m$ and $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ with $p = 18\,000\text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of about 20. The correct speed is $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$, which gives a much larger $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$.

C.explanation: Correct. With $v = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $E_k = \frac{1}{2} \times 1200 \times 15^2 = 135\,000\text{ J} = 135\text{ kJ}$.

D.explanation: Exactly twice the correct value. It comes from using $p^2/m$ instead of $p^2/(2m)$, omitting the $\frac{1}{2}$ in kinetic energy.

hints: Start from the two given numbers: $m = 1200\text{ kg}$ and $p = 18\,000\text{ kg m s}^{-1}$. Momentum must first give you the speed $v$.
Recall the two linked equations $p = mv$ and $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$, which combine to $E_k = p^2/(2m)$.
Calculate $v = 18\,000/1200$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$, then substitute into $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ and convert the joule result to $\text{kJ}$ by dividing by $1000$.
walkthrough: Identify the useful data: mass $m = 1200\text{ kg}$ and magnitude of momentum $p = 18\,000\text{ kg m s}^{-1}$. Velocity is not given, so it must be found first.
Use $p = mv$ rearranged to $v = p/m$. Substitute: $v = 18\,000/1200 = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
State the kinetic energy rule: $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$. Alternatively $E_k = p^2/(2m)$ gives the same result directly.
Substitute with units: $E_k = \frac{1}{2} \times 1200\text{ kg} \times (15\text{ m s}^{-1})^2$.
Evaluate: $(15)^2 = 225$, so $E_k = 600 \times 225 = 135\,000\text{ J}$. Check units: $\text{kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2} = \text{J}$.
Convert to kilojoules: $135\,000/1000 = 135\text{ kJ}$. This is option C.
